MCP Server

Best for: Claude, Cursor, Windsurf, any MCP-compatible AI agent

Install

# Add to your MCP config (claude_desktop_config.json, etc.)
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "pumpclaw": {
      "command": "npx",
      "args": ["pumpclaw-mcp"],
      "env": {
        "BASE_PRIVATE_KEY": "your-private-key",
        "BASE_RPC_URL": "https://base-rpc.publicnode.com"
      }
    }
  }
}

Available Tools

  • create_token — Deploy a new ERC-20 with instant Uniswap V4 liquidity
  • list_tokens — Browse all PumpClaw tokens on-chain
  • get_token — Get details for a specific token

Usage

// Your agent simply says:
"Create a token called DogeClaw with symbol DCLAW and 1 billion supply"

// The MCP server handles everything:
// → Deploys ERC-20 contract
// → Creates Uniswap V4 pool
// → Locks liquidity forever
// → Returns token address + trade links

CLI

Best for: Scripts, CI/CD, shell-based agents, one-off deploys

One-Command Deploy

# Interactive mode — walks you through everything
npx pumpclaw-cli deploy

# Non-interactive — perfect for scripts
npx pumpclaw-cli deploy \
  --name "MyToken" \
  --symbol "MTK" \
  --supply 1000000000 \
  --private-key $BASE_PRIVATE_KEY \
  --rpc https://base-rpc.publicnode.com

Other Commands

# List all PumpClaw tokens
npx pumpclaw-cli list

# Get token details
npx pumpclaw-cli info 0xYourTokenAddress
📦 npm: npmjs.com/package/pumpclaw-cli — Zero dependencies, works everywhere Node.js runs.

Direct Contract Call

Best for: Custom integrations, other smart contracts, maximum control

Factory Contract

// Factory: 0xe5bCa0eDe9208f7Ee7FCAFa0415Ca3DC03e16a90 (Base)
// ABI: createToken(string name, string symbol, string imageUrl,
//                   uint256 totalSupply, uint256 initialFdv, address creator)

import { createPublicClient, createWalletClient, http } from 'viem'
import { base } from 'viem/chains'
import { privateKeyToAccount } from 'viem/accounts'

const FACTORY = '0xe5bCa0eDe9208f7Ee7FCAFa0415Ca3DC03e16a90'
const account = privateKeyToAccount(`0x${process.env.BASE_PRIVATE_KEY}`)

const wallet = createWalletClient({
  account, chain: base, transport: http('https://base-rpc.publicnode.com')
})

const tx = await wallet.writeContract({
  address: FACTORY,
  abi: [{
    name: 'createToken',
    type: 'function',
    inputs: [
      { name: 'name', type: 'string' },
      { name: 'symbol', type: 'string' },
      { name: 'imageUrl', type: 'string' },
      { name: 'totalSupply', type: 'uint256' },
      { name: 'initialFdv', type: 'uint256' },
      { name: 'creator', type: 'address' },
    ],
    outputs: [{ type: 'address' }],
    stateMutability: 'nonpayable'
  }],
  functionName: 'createToken',
  args: [
    'My Agent Token',
    'MAT',
    'https://example.com/logo.png',
    parseUnits('1000000000', 18),  // 1B supply
    parseEther('20'),              // ~$50k starting FDV
    account.address                   // creator gets 80% of fees
  ]
})
📄 Full ABI + docs: github.com/clawd800/pumpclaw
4

GitHub Action

Best for: CI/CD pipelines, automated deploys on release, GitHub-native agents

Workflow Example

# .github/workflows/deploy-token.yml
name: Deploy Token
on: workflow_dispatch

jobs:
  deploy:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: clawd800/pumpclaw-action@v1
        id: token
        with:
          name: 'My Agent Token'
          symbol: 'MAT'
          private-key: ${{ secrets.BASE_PRIVATE_KEY }}

      - run: echo "Token: ${{ steps.token.outputs.token-address }}"
🎬 GitHub: clawd800/pumpclaw-action — Deploy tokens directly from GitHub Actions. Auto-generates DexScreener + Matcha links.

Why PumpClaw?

  • Free — Zero ETH to deploy. Just gas (~$0.30).
  • 80% creator fees — Every swap on your token's Uniswap V4 pool sends 80% of fees to the creator address. (Clanker gives 40%.)
  • LP locked forever — Liquidity goes into a non-removable Uniswap V4 position. No rugs.
  • Instant trading — Token is tradeable on Uniswap, Matcha, DexScreener, and GeckoTerminal immediately after deployment.
  • On-chain registry — All tokens indexed on-chain. No database, no API keys, no rate limits.
  • Agent-first — Built for programmatic use. MCP, CLI, and raw contract calls all first-class.
